question_text:
In Cu, if we assume that each Cu atom donates one electron, the free electron concentration is $8.5 \times 10^{22} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$. (a) What is the value of $E_{\mathrm{F}, 0}$? (b) If the concentration of conduction electrons estimated by conductivity measurements is $1.5 \times 10^{23} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$, then find the number of electrons donated per Cu atom. Give your answer as a tuple (Fermi energy at 0K, number of electrons donated per Cu atom).

Refer to Table:
Fermi Energy Levels ( $E_{F, 0}$ ) and Work Functions ( $\phi$ ) for Different Metals
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline Metal & Work Function ( $\phi$ ) ( eV ) & Fermi Energy Level at $0 \mathrm{~K}\left(E_{F, 0}\right)$ \\
\hline Silver & 4.26 & 5.5 \\
\hline Aluminum & 4.28 & 11.7 \\
\hline Gold & 5.1 & 5.5 \\
\hline Copper & 4.65 & 7.0 \\
\hline Lithium & 2.3 & 4.7 \\
\hline Magnesium & 3.7 & 7.1 \\
\hline Sodium & 2.75 & 3.2 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}The units of each required answer are (eV, ), respectively.
response:
## Reasoning

### Part (a): Fermi Energy at 0 K

The Fermi energy for a free electron gas is:

$$E_{F,0} = \frac{h^2}{8m}\left(\frac{3n}{\pi}\right)^{2/3}$$

With $n = 8.5 \times 10^{22}\,\text{cm}^{-3} = 8.5 \times 10^{28}\,\text{m}^{-3}$, $h = 6.626\times10^{-34}$ J·s, $m = 9.109\times10^{-31}$ kg:

$$E_{F,0} \approx 1.13\times10^{-18}\,\text{J} \approx 7.05\,\text{eV} \approx 7.0\,\text{eV}$$

This matches the table value for Copper ($E_{F,0} = 7.0$ eV). ✓

### Part (b): Electrons donated per Cu atom

The atomic concentration of Cu is $8.5 \times 10^{22}\,\text{cm}^{-3}$ (one electron per atom). The conductivity-based conduction electron concentration is $1.5 \times 10^{23}\,\text{cm}^{-3}$.

$$\text{electrons per atom} = \frac{1.5\times10^{23}}{8.5\times10^{22}} = \frac{1.5}{0.85} \approx 1.76$$

## Answer

$$\boxed{(7.0,\ 1.76)}$$
